causes.title: Retaking an ally's capital from the enemy scores as the conquest of an enemy capital: +15 alarm, a plunder prompt and the Threat to 100/100 in one turn
causes.prior: sibling of DDB-42 (a province the capturer holds title to is recovered, not conquered), CA8-13 (no plunder modal on own soil) and PT-F1 (an ally-HELD province is not ours to take) — all present; none was widened to an ALLY's soil retaken from the enemy, the other side of the same class (Rule 10)
causes.cause: Three arms treat the liberation of an ally's ground as a conquest. (a) `world_state.py:5203-5219`: +2 `region_capture` unless the starting controller is the capturer or `capture_recovers_title` (`:1398`) — Munich is Bavaria's starting province, taken by Austria, so France is neither. (b) `combat_executor.py:5494-5497`: +15 `capital_capture` whenever `conquered` and `is_capital`, with no check of whose capital; the label "Captured an enemy capital" is `diplomatic_ledger.py:110`. (c) `_attempt_region_capture` (`combat_executor.py:12744-12790`) skips the plunder/secure modal only for `is_own_soil_recapture` (`world_state.py:897`, France's starting soil), so Munich offered "Plunder it for 1,200 gold" (action 57) and the capture handed Munich to France. PT-F1's `_pursuit_capture_guard` (`:12618-12662`, "not ours to take") covers only an ally-HELD province, which is why Swabia read correctly at action 10; `game_end.ally_homeland_returns` (`:926`) returns the province only at a peace. Also: `_alarm_line` (`:6506-6509`) prints the applied total (+8, clipped by the cap at 100) beside the raw parts (+2 +3 +5 +15 = 25). The player: Ney with the whole army attacked Archduke Charles at Munich (turn 3), Bavaria's capital Austria had just taken from the ally, and drove him out; the report said "Europe's alarm rises +8 … Captured an enemy capital +15" and the top bar's Threat went 84 → 100/100. Verified on the source (`world_state.py:5203-5219`, `combat_executor.py:5494-5497`).
causes.fix: One predicate `liberates_ally_ground(world, region, capturer)` (the province's home nation, `game_end.home_nation_of`, is an ally or client of the capturer and the province is taken from an enemy), read by all three arms and the AI's capture path (Rule 5); the capital's label names it ("Munich, Bavaria's capital, retaken"); `_alarm_line` prints each row's applied share or "(capped at 100)". The design half (S14G-D1): does the liberation hand the province back to the ally at once or hold it until the peace.
causes.dr: Should retaking an ALLY's province from the enemy be a liberation — handed back to the ally at once, no plunder prompt, no conquest alarm — or stay a conquest of France's until the peace sorts it out?

causes.title: An aggressive marshal drops a standing "support Napoleon" order at the turn change and rushes alone to another man's battle, and no order reply says he will
causes.prior: sibling of S14E-7 (End Turn's army line, which fired and named the pairing) and SR-2e AAR-9 (the interrupt's lawful branch); both fixes are in the tree (`19319041`, `6e288d57`) — this is the lawful branch AAR-9 leaves open, and nothing says so at the order
causes.cause: `strategic.py:4903` `_check_interrupts` runs for every order type (`:2300`, `:3302`, before the order's own handler); only "literal" is exempt (`:4916`). Massena is `"personality": "aggressive"` (`europe_1805.json:249`). At `:4951-4960` `if personality == "aggressive" and lawful:` returns a redirect; `_handle_interrupt` (`:4984-5111`) walks him to the battle province and sets `marshal.strategic_order = None` (`:5088`); the message is "hears cannon fire! Abandoning orders — rushing to Hungary!" (`:5103`). `lawful` (`:1318`) is true because Kutuzov, at war with France, stood at Hungary (`:1329-1331`), within the two-province range (`:4936`). Nothing tests morale or odds. The SUPPORT reply (`strategic_executor.py:2394-2402`) promises only a march to Napoleon's battles; only the PURSUE reply says "may be diverted by an interrupt" (`:2336`); the same silence is in the MOVE_TO reply (`:2302-2309`), HOLD (`:2340-2353`) and FOLLOW (`:2354-2363`). The S14E-7 gate (`dispatch.py:4570-4633`) fired correctly ("morale below 40% beside Kutuzov") but names the pairing, not that his standing order would carry him into it. The player: Massena (22,000, morale 36%) on a standing "support Napoleon" at Bohemia, the army massed for the assault on Vienna; at the turn change "Massena hears cannon fire! Abandoning orders — rushing to Hungary!" — alone, next to Kutuzov's 33,000, 327 men lost to the march.
causes.fix: Keep the mechanic — it is the character (DDB-D1: temperament in the line, never in acting unordered; here the order says it). For an aggressive marshal append one sentence to the MOVE_TO / HOLD / SUPPORT / FOLLOW replies: "he will drop this order for any battle within two provinces in a war of ours"; add a second End Turn gate clause naming an aggressive corps with a standing order and a known enemy beside it. The design half (S14G-D2): does a supporter of the Emperor leave him for another man's guns.
causes.dr: Should an aggressive marshal on a standing SUPPORT / MOVE / HOLD order leave it for any battle within two provinces — alone, at 36% morale — or should the order he was given hold him?

causes.title: "Support Napoleon" lapses or follows according to the supporter's NAME: Davout and Lannes stop, Ney follows the Emperor home across Europe
causes.prior: NEW; a sibling of AO's FOLLOW distinction (`standing_follow`, `64e2fc70`) and CA9-F8's reply text — both present, neither covers the processing order. Its consequence is conquest #9's turn-11 reading (S14G-17)
causes.cause: A supporter not co-located with his ally walks to him every tick (`strategic.py:4748-4845`; the comment at `:4756` "SUPPORT silently follows"; the message "moves to support … 0 regions away" at `:4841`). The "lapses of itself" rule the reply promises sits only in the co-located branch (`:4689`, the lapse arm `:4731`) and is evaluated at the supporter's own tick — and `process_strategic_orders` processes the player's marshals ALPHABETICALLY (`:2115`, `sorted(..., key=lambda m: m.name)`, verified): Davout and Lannes sort before Napoleon, see him still at Dresden and lapse ("Napoleon is secure", turn 12); Ney sorts after, finds Napoleon already gone and follows him every turn until the player re-ordered him. The reply (`strategic_executor.py:2394-2402`) says "when Napoleon leads a battle within reach, he will march to the guns. The order lapses of itself once Napoleon is out of danger" and never says the supporter follows a moving ally. SUPPORT costs 1 AP (SR-2e), so players use it as a cheap group move. The player: on turn 9 Ney, Lannes and Davout "support Napoleon" to move them to Moravia; on turn 10 Napoleon marched alone toward Normandy; at the turn change all three moved to Dresden after him ("Davout moves to support Napoleon. 0 regions away.") and then followed his seven-turn road home, 1,406 men lost to supply at Dresden.
causes.fix: Run the "ally is safe" lapse AFTER the follow move in `_execute_support` (`strategic.py:4828`), so a plain support lapses on arrival for every supporter alike (or process supporters after their ally); the reply says what it does: "goes to him now and stays only while he is in danger — 'follow Napoleon' keeps him at your side."

causes.title: A march order for the province the corps already stands in is accepted, spends an action and replaces the standing order — and the dispatch's "HALTED … awaiting your word" stays on the page after "Continue as Ordered" has answered it
causes.verdict: defect (the redundant order); the claim as filed was a misreading
causes.prior: NEW (S14E-30, which puts the dispatch before the question, is present and worked as built); class-link to conquest #8 / S14G-3 ("0 regions away") — an order with an empty path accepted
causes.cause: The row as filed — "Continue as Ordered halted Napoleon's march" — is a misreading: Napoleon DID arrive (action 33 replies "Napoleon arrives at Flanders"; the map piece moved; the Turn 4 dispatch says Flanders). The dispatch (action 31, `frames/0031.jpg`) was built after the advance raised the cannon-fire interrupt, so it reads "Napoleon — Orleanais — HALTED at Orleanais — awaiting your word"; S14E-30 deliberately shows the dispatch before the question (`main.gd:7466-7475`), and `continue_order` (`strategic.py:2752-2798`) then stepped him on; nothing retracts the line, which stays in the scrollback beside the arrival. The real defect is what followed: at action 38 the player typed "Napoleon, march to Flanders" (he already stood there) and it was accepted, charged 1 AP ("[3/4 actions remaining]") and "arrived" on the next tick (action 47). `strategic_executor.py:1515` `if dest and dest != ctx.marshal.location:` skips the road stage, but nothing refuses a same-province destination; the order is created at `:1895-1937` and replied at `:2302-2306`, and it silently replaces any standing order; the plain `move` refuses it (`movement_executor.py:569`, "is already in", verified).
causes.fix: Refuse a MOVE_TO whose destination is the marshal's own province, free ("Napoleon already stands at Flanders — nothing spent"), at `_strategic_path`; mark the own province not-a-destination in `order_quotes.march_quote` / `march_roads` (`_standing_quote` `:269-277` quotes it as ok today); and mark an interrupt's dispatch line answered once the player answers it ("HALTED at Orleanais — answered: continued").

causes.title: A marshal's audience card names a quarry that has since gone ("against Mack into Munich") and sends him, alone, at whoever is weakest in reach — announced only after the actions and the battle
causes.prior: NEW; sibling of the A3 stale-answer guard (it re-derives availability, not the shown quarry) and DDB-17 (the card silent that he goes alone)
causes.cause: `jealousy.py:2152-2182` `_command_option` bakes the card's detail ("Send him against Mack into Munich") at build time, in the previous turn's pass; `refresh_petition_affordability` (`:2801-2893`) re-derives only `enabled` and `unavailable_reason`, never the `detail` or the quarry. At action 57 Ney beat Mack ("Mack's broken army flees to Tyrol!"); at action 62 the tooltip still named Mack; on the click (action 63) `_apply_command_choice` (`:3735-3807`) re-derives the quarry through `find_autonomous_attack_target` (`:4776`, the weakest enemy in or adjacent to his province): Archduke Charles at Franconia (31,690 against Murat's 18,920), and runs PURSUE with `objection_response="proceed"`. The first-step gate is structurally dead on this path (docstring `:3752`) and the odds gate that autonomous glory attacks obey (`glory_attack_held_by_the_odds`, `:263`, used at `:4873`) is not applied; the switch is announced only after the 2 AP and the battle (`:3798` "Archduke Charles, then."); "Ney never came" is the generic grievance line. The player lost 5,379 men to Charles's 2,632, alone, on a target the card did not name. The dispatch warning "Murat is eyeing Mack's position at Munich" (`:4628`) is re-targeted silently at fire time (`:4851`) the same way.
causes.fix: Re-run `_command_option` in `refresh_petition_affordability`; in `_apply_command_choice`, if the live quarry differs from the card's, spend nothing and ask: "Mack has left Munich; Archduke Charles at Franconia (~31,690 against 18,920) is all that is in reach — send him?" with the muster and the odds reading (the gate autonomous glory attacks obey).

causes.title: "Not Now" on an envoy's letter leaves the Cabinet shut, and the lock is stated only in tooltips and after the click — a routine lesser-court letter shuts it too
causes.prior: RETURN (partial) of S14E-18 — its fix is present (`utils.gd:509` `cabinet_shut_line`, `4ac79a0f`) and fired on both roads: the sentence is on the Not Now tooltip, the Cabinet button's tooltip, the wizard notice and the post-click echo; it says the lock, it neither removes it nor puts it on the button's face or in the letter
causes.cause: The lock is deliberate: `dialogue_manager.has_current_turn_offers` (`dialogue_manager.py:667-683`) over `CURRENT_TURN_OFFER_TYPES` (`:111-120`) feeds `dialogue_pending`; every `incoming_proposal` counts, including the routine lesser-court Open Borders letters of the Ottoman Empire and Portugal (diplomacy #11: three minor-court letters shut the Cabinet on every turn envoys arrived), while a moment letter does not (`:673-679`). The sentence "Set this letter aside — the Cabinet stays shut until it is answered or the turn ends." lives on the Not Now tooltip (`incoming_proposal_popup.gd:283-287`), the Cabinet button's tooltip (`main.gd:6148`), the wizard's notice (`diplomacy_wizard.gd:1758`) and the post-click echo (`main.gd:7853`); `_set_cabinet_locked` (`main.gd:6131-6150`) writes only the tooltip and `_cabinet_locked` (`:311`, `:6146`) has no reader (verified by grep); the Envoys badge's tooltip (`top_bar.gd:762`) says "3 pending envoys await your reply" and never the Cabinet; the popup body never states it. The players: conquest pressed Not Now on Austria's armistice (turn 5) to deal with the Hanover crisis and found the Cabinet shut — "nothing on the Not Now button says it" (half wrong: the tooltip does); diplomacy tried the Cabinet on turn 2 with three envoys unanswered and met a greyed button (the grey at actions 42-43 was the enemy-phase modal disabling input, `main.gd:6407`, not the lock; at action 44 only the tooltip had changed).
causes.fix: Put the lock in visible text: a line under the letter's buttons ("Set aside — the Cabinet stays shut until it is answered or the turn ends") and "(Cabinet stays shut)" on the Not Now label; `Utils.cabinet_shut_line` also in the Envoys badge tooltip and the letter's body; read `_cabinet_locked` to style the Cabinet button's face ("The Cabinet — shut", amber). The design half (S14G-D3): which letters lock.
causes.dr: Should EVERY unanswered envoy letter shut the Cabinet for the turn — a minor court's routine Open Borders letter as much as an armistice from Austria — or only the letters that carry a decision the player must make before treating?

causes.title: An armistice with Austria leaves Bavaria's war running: Austria takes the ground under the French corps, Berthier marches them home, and the terms said only a count
causes.prior: RETURN (partial) of SFR-D28 (its scenario — Austria stormed Munich and Swabia under the truce — recurred on two roads; the announce half is present, `allies_whose_war_runs_on`, `91c85e43`, and fired, but states a count, not the consequence); siblings `separate_peace_words` (`diplomacy.py:6579`) and S14E-4's sanctuary line share the pattern
causes.cause: The preview said it — "Bavaria stays at war with Austria under this truce … her war runs on, and 7 [5 on the sea road] French corps stand on Bavarian soil under the truce" (`diplomacy.py:3286-3340` `allies_whose_war_runs_on` / `truce_followers_line`, the WARNING row at `:6718-6737`) — as one bullet among many: the count, not the consequence. Under an ARMISTICE France is not at war with Austria, so the corps cannot fight for the ally; the enemy phase of the next turn showed Austria storming Munich and Swabia with the corps standing there (Bavaria eliminated on the sea road). A province that changes hands strands the corps (`dispatch.py:7860-7862`: "Ney and Davout stand on Swabia, now Austria's soil … they may march out, but no corps of ours may enter it again"; `withdrawal.py:1431-1434`), and Berthier's road-home orders (`offer_road_home`, `:1041-1127`; deliberately free and automatic) march them out — "put on the road home to Nivernais; 5 turns of safe passage" — so one dispatch says "may march out" and "already marched". The sea player's 2-AP march to Swabia ordered AFTER the accept got no warning at the order and bought no distance (`movement_executor.py:371-395` has foreign-soil notes for pay, supply and camp, none for "this soil is a front"). The players: diplomacy accepted a 51-of-50 armistice on turn 3 and lost Munich and Swabia on turn 4, Berthier sending Ney, Davout and Murat home without an order; the sea road accepted Austria's "GENEROUS" armistice on turn 7 and saw its five corps leave Bavaria and Bavaria eliminated.
causes.fix: Add the consequence to the `war_runs_on` display and `truce_followers_line` (`diplomacy.py:6730-6733`, `:3338`) and lead the confirm with the row: "your corps will not fight for her; Austria may take her provinces where they stand, and ground that changes hands puts them on the road home — Berthier marches them out (N turns of safe passage) and none may enter again"; a one-line front note beside `campaign_pay_note` on a march into an ally province an armistice partner is attacking; the dispatch says they are already marching.

causes.title: Talleyrand's "Satisfy their design (Britain)" counsel opens a generic standstill menu whose "Propose peace" sends a plain 3-DP treaty — the design is never put on the table
causes.prior: sibling of DDB-9 (the menu's sends — `_stamp_menu_sends`, `diplomatic_dialogue.py:1722`, present, handles only the refusal), S14E-26 (`buyoff_quote`, `instruments.py:1290`, present — the quote-first sweep never listed this menu) and DDB-4
causes.cause: The counsel (`diplomatic_advisory.py:520-530`, label "Satisfy their design", tooltip "open talks and put it on the table") becomes action `expand_options` carrying only `target_nation` (`:1137-1143`): the design's title and covet list are dropped. `diplomatic_executor.py:6193-6223` re-routes it as a vague proposal to the T3 template ("war … at a standstill", `diplomatic_templates.py:786-810`). The option descriptions render only as tooltips (`proposal_confirm_popup.gd:286-293`), so the body is empty; "Propose peace" is an `execute_proposal` whose terms are never shown (`diplomatic_dialogue.py:1416-1443`) and it sends at once (`diplomatic_executor.py:5399-5474`, 3 DP deducted at `:5474`). The menu type gets no acceptance estimate or DP price (enrichment runs only for confirm/execute, `diplomatic_dialogue.py:1527`). A coveted province is added to the terms only when `war_score < -20` (`diplomatic_templates.py:3712`), so at +0 the "peace" cannot satisfy the design. The player (turn 1): Talleyrand advised "Satisfy their design (Britain)" at high confidence; the button opened "war with Britain is at a standstill — Propose peace / Press advantage / Wait" with a large empty body and no mention of the design or of odds; "Propose peace" silently spent 3 of the 5 DP on a plain Peace Treaty to Britain (the Cabinet had called such an offer "Hopeless" for Austria).
causes.fix: Route the "Satisfy their design" rung to a `proposal_confirm` pre-loaded with the coveted-province cession (terms, acceptance band and DP shown), or make the menu's "Propose peace" open `proposal_confirm` instead of sending, with each option's DP and terms in the body; the siblings are the other `open_proposal` counsels that land on this menu (`diplomatic_advisory.py:370, 459, 536, 546, 641`) and templates T2/T4/T5 (`diplomatic_templates.py:755-873`).

causes.title: Two buy-offs (about 2,300 gold) leave Britain and Russia "she would join" the next league; the page says the design sleeps, not that the court still counts
causes.prior: sibling of S14E-26 (the buy-off quote — present, silent on the league) and DDB-31; NEW as a league-page row (SF-LB-3)
causes.cause: League membership is `qualifies_for_coalition` (`coalition.py:1838-1879`: relation below −10, the fresh-peace and cooldown checks); it never reads a sleeping design. A buy-off does two things: it sleeps the design 15 turns and adds +5 relation (`instruments.py:59, 521-545`); `league_forecast` prices that +5 as a league lever (`coalition.py:4237-4248`, text `:4304-4330`). The page footer (`diplomatic_ledger.py:1556-1560`) says only "puts the design to sleep 15 turns"; `buyoff_quote` (`instruments.py:1290-1310`) likewise omits the +5 and that the court still counts toward the league; `compute_buyoff_price` returns None once no design is live (`:390-398`), so the clause just vanishes. NOT FOUND: any builder showing which bargains are in force or their `expires_turn`. `dispatch.py:776` ("a court bought off now is a regiment the league never fields") contradicts the predicate. The player paid 1,116 g + 1 DP (Britain), 1,152 g + 1 DP (Russia) and later 1,008 g + 1 DP (Austria) on turn 7; on turn 11 the dispatch said "Britain and Russia would now join a league against us", the Balance page still listed both as "she would join" and priced the way out at the same relations road (8 and 7 turns of Talleyrand) as before (9 and 8) — one turn shorter.
causes.fix: Add to `buyoff_quote` and the Balance footer: "+5 relations; she still counts toward a league until relations reach −10"; print "design bought off, N turns left" on that court's league row (read `compensation_bargains.expires_turn`); correct the `dispatch.py:776` sentence. The design half (S14G-D6): should a bought-off court leave the league table.
causes.dr: Should a court whose design has been bought off (asleep 15 turns) still count toward a league against France while its relations stand under −10?

causes.title: The licence's quote omits what the licensed war costs: Prussia's declaration drops her relations with every court, France's included, and undoes the courtship under way
causes.prior: sibling of S14E-9 (`declaration_cost_to_player`, `diplomacy.py:10679`, present — it fired at action 212, after the fact) and S14E-26 (quote-first fired at action 90): neither joins the quote to the declaration it licenses; class-link to conquest #10 (a consequence unpriced at the choice)
causes.cause: `sponsorship_quote`'s licence branch (`instruments.py:1326-1331`) states the 1 DP, "pledges non-interference for 10 turns" and the renege bond (−25); nothing of the war it licenses. When the licensee declares, `diplomacy.py:10954-10963` applies `declaration_relation_penalties` (`:10670-10676`, −15 indirect, halved with a casus belli) to the AGGRESSOR's relations with every court that is neither party — France's included, so France–Prussia falls 15 (action 212: "Relations now at 2 (+16 earned, −15 from Prussia's declaration …)"). The player's "lowers everyone's opinion of me" overstates it: it is PRUSSIA's relations with every court that fall, and the loss France feels is the Prussia courtship it had running (+18 → +2). `declaration_cost_clause` (`:10737-10744`) has no subject ("relations with every court, France's included, fall 15"); `commitments_routing.py:384` (the break clause) has the same subjectless sentence; `guarantee_quote` (`instruments.py:1341`) and the buy-off quote (`:1290`) name no later third-party cost either. The player granted the licence on turn 4 ("no gold, 1 diplomatic point"; the confirmation box talked only of reneging), declined to stop the war on turn 10, and on turn 11 read "Prussia has declared war on Hanover — relations with every court, France's included, fall 15".
causes.fix: In `sponsorship_quote` (the licence and the sponsor): "If {licensee} then declares on {aim}, her relations with every court, France's included, fall 15 (France–{licensee} now +10 → −5); any Improve Relations running there is undone", computed from `declaration_relation_penalties` and the live mission; give `declaration_cost_clause` and the `commitments_routing.py:384` clause a subject ("Prussia's relations with every court …").

causes.title: A march to Flanders crosses Prussia's armed-neutral ground — Open Borders does not exempt it — and costs −25 with Prussia with no word at the order
causes.prior: sibling of S14E-22 (the typed march's detour ask) and S14E-23 (Open Borders' effect line) — both present (`4ac79a0f`); neither reaches a guarded province: `march_detour_reading` returns None unless the direct road is closed
causes.cause: `agendas.py:1248-1354` `process_agenda_violations` fires −25 (`:49`) when a belligerent's marshal stands in a region of an ACTIVE `guard_neutrality` agenda (Prussia's: Hanover, Westphalia, Brunswick, Berlin and Brandenburg, `europe_1805.json:953-958`); the exemptions are open war or armistice, allies, a lord or client, and one's own soil (`:1310-1324`, verified) — Open Borders is not one, though its letter says "each side's armies may cross the other's provinces" (`display_names.py:1875`). The march reply prints only "Route: …" (`strategic_executor.py:2308-2309`); `march_detour_reading` (`strategic.py:1097`) returns None at `:1131-1136` unless the direct road is closed, so S14E-22's open-borders arm never ran; the shift line "takes up a new design: Armed Neutrality" carries only the title (`agendas.py:1491-1497`; the stance line exists only in the Diplomacy ledger, `:1425`). The Ansbach trap is by design (`NATION_AGENDAS_SPEC` §5.9); the price is unstated at the order. The player: on turn 10 "Soult, march to Flanders" answered "Route: Dresden → Berlin → Brunswick → Amsterdam → Flanders"; Prussia had taken up Armed Neutrality the same turn; on turn 13 "Prussia seethes: France's columns cross Brunswick in defiance of its declared neutrality" — −17 that turn, −25 in Talleyrand's report, the relation at −32, a courting mission undone, an Open Borders signed on turn 2 notwithstanding.
causes.fix: Factor the guard map out of `process_agenda_violations`; add `march_guard_reading(world, marshal, road)` beside `march_detour_reading` as a free ask and a reply rider: "Berlin and Brunswick are Prussia's guarded ground — standing in them costs −25 with Prussia — march, go round or cancel?"; put the clause in the "Armed Neutrality" shift beat and the open_borders effect line. Siblings: the other guard decks (Denmark/Holstein, Poland's Posen/Lithuania/Volhynia, Ulster/Munster), and every order whose road passes a guarded province.

causes.title: The table's gold ceiling (1,000g, 26 of 50) is stated on a line the header never shows, and the standing hint "use More generous until each accepts" is false there
causes.verdict: design+legibility (+ a defect in the [+] sibling)
causes.prior: RETURN (partial) of DDB-33 (the ceiling and its note are present, `33643c45`) and G4F-5 (the beat carrier, `4ad7aaf9`): the note exists and the screen does not show it; sibling of S14E-6 (the legitimacy refusal's guard) and DDB-7 (a below-the-fold cue that exists only in `diplomacy_wizard.gd:96`)
causes.cause: A real, deliberate ceiling whose wording is hidden. The scorer credits France's gold to a court at 1 point per 25g, capped at 40 points = 1,000g (`settlement_scoring.py:563-564`, `:1811`); the dial stops there (`settlement_staging.py:1431-1439`, `:1450-1456`). Britain's blocker is the player-authored "Erect Ireland" demand (term harshness −23, legitimacy −20), an identity clause the dial passes through (`:1520-1522`); gold alone tops out at 17 + 9 = 26 of 50. The note IS authored — "Gold past 1,000 buys nothing more from Britain at this table, Sire." (`:1603-1609`), shipped as an `authoring_voice_beat` (`settlement_actions.py:776-784`; replies at actions 266 and 271) — but invisible: the popup draws it as the LAST line of the header (`proposal_confirm_popup.gd:1137-1148`, `:271`), a `scroll_active`, `fit_content = false` RichTextLabel (`proposal_confirm_popup.tscn:57-64`) that shows about nine lines at 5120×1440; the state holds the line (`state/0266.json`) but frames 0266, 0272 and 0278 show nothing after "I'd ease Britain …"; the Castlereagh beat (action 262) is hidden the same way. The standing hint "Use 'More generous' … until each accepts" (`settlement_staging.py:1873-1901`) pivots only for a treasury bound (PF-1) or a legitimacy mismatch (S14E-6, guard at `settlement_actions.py:484-486`), so it is false here. The gold [+] was NOT dead: it is `[url=mag:…:amount:+]` (`proposal_confirm_popup.gd:1294`) and would have set 1,100g; the player's click at (1758, 530) missed it (it sits near (1591, 374)), and the instrument never listed it (`dd_b_client.gd:81-82, 845-847` strips bracketed link text — S14G-I1). The real defect beside it: the per-line [+] has no ceiling and spends gold that buys nothing (`settlement_actions.py:1188-1207`, `settlement_staging.py:585-599`). causes.title: The screens print "Press G / T to close" but the command line keeps the caret, so the bare key types into it
causes.verdict: defect (the advertised key is dead in the game's dominant state)

causes.cause: `marshal_management.gd:285` says "Press G to close." Opening a screen does not move focus off the command line (`main.gd:1468-1469`); after every reply `set_input_enabled(true)` grabs focus (`main.gd:6394-6414`); the Escape ladder closes the topmost thing and "the line keeps focus" (`_escape_closes_topmost`, `main.gd:1656`, the battle rung `:1671-1673`, the line's Esc arm `:1441-1462`); `_is_hotkey_blocked()` is `command_input.has_focus() or modal` (`main.gd:7961-7963`), so a bare letter types into the line, and only Alt+key is intercepted while typing (`:1386-1392`). States 0030 (conquest) and 0035 (diplomacy) show `editing: true, focused: true` and the stray letter in the line. The boot help promises "the bare keys work whenever you are not typing" (`main.gd:1119`) and captions say "Ledger (T)" (`top_bar.gd:175`); the only cue is the placeholder "(Type command…)". The same unswept copy: `strategic_ledger.gd:362` "press T to close it", `dispatch_view.gd:129` "Press R to reread", and about 41 backend strings "press T/G/D/L/R/N" (14 in `counsel.py` `_SURFACE_FOR_KIND`, 8 in `meta_executor.py`, 5 in `naval_executor.py`, 4 in `first_contact.py`, `naval.py:361`). The players: conquest pressed G to close the Generals screen (turn 2) and a "g" landed in the line; diplomacy pressed Escape on a battle picture and then T for the Ledger and a "t" landed (every time a picture or pop-up was closed with Escape).
causes.fix: When `_escape_closes_topmost` closes a modal, screen or picture and the line is empty, `release_focus()` (the placeholder then reads "Esc: menu · click to type"); re-copy the close hints as "Esc closes it (Alt+G while you type)"; route the backend pointers through one helper that appends "(Alt+X while you type)" as S14D-X28 did for the digit.

causes.title: The Admiralty readied an inland corps to embark on turn 10 and asked for a march to a yard on turn 11, with no reason printed

causes.title: "No marshal of infantry can reach Normandy" — then "Dumonceau commands our foot at Normandy" — then "his men belong to Holland"
causes.prior: sibling of SF5-RV1 (`levy_passes_over`, `d1018208`, present at `economy_executor.py:539`, `:2129`, `world_state.py:6785`) — RV1 claimed "all six levy sites" and missed these two CN-2 helpers
causes.cause: Two helpers disagree. The selector `world_state.py:6785-6787` `ready_marshals_near(for_levy=True)` passes over a serving contingent through `contingent.levy_passes_over` (`contingent.py:346`), so Dumonceau (Holland's contingent) is excluded and the sentence says "none of ours stands within reach" (`economy_executor.py:797-799`). The remedy `recruit_arm_remedy` (`economy_executor.py:703-731`) builds `serving` straight from `world.marshals` WITHOUT `levy_passes_over` (verified) and names him at distance 0 with the unconditional "march him within reach, or give him the order yourself" (`:730`); `named_arm_refusal` (`:758-776`) has the same unfiltered list; `_recruit_quote_core` returns the same remedy as the chip's `remedy` (`:894`). The player (turn 14): "recruit infantry in Normandy" → the first reply, then "Dumonceau, recruit infantry" as the game suggested → the second; he stood at Normandy already, so "march him within reach" meant nothing.
causes.fix: Filter `serving` through `levy_passes_over` in both helpers; `_msg_no_arm_in_range` prints the blocked reason ("Dumonceau commands our foot here, but Holland pays its men — recruit into one of our own corps"); skip "march him within reach" when the man is already at the province.

causes.title: End Turn warns "2 corps stand in peril — an enemy force of ~29,126 shares the field" about an army that has left
causes.prior: RETURN (partial) of S14E-X31 (IN PERIL at the click, fixed in S14f part 2) — the clause exists (`dispatch.py:4636`, `main.py:802`) but reads the frozen snapshot instead of the live sighting; related S14E-7 (the sibling army line, `dispatch.py:4570`, reads live through `get_visible_enemies` and `intel_surfaces.sighting_row`)

The gate therefore prints yesterday's label (`intel_surfaces.py:280-293` already calls a frozen FULL label naming an absent man "yesterday's"). causes.title: The Turn 6 dispatch says "the war with Bavaria and Prussia is over" — France was at war with neither
causes.prior: NEW; sibling of SFR-D43 / RR3-X13 (the "truce vs war is over" words — `treaty_word` is present but binary); downstream of S14G-7's stranding
causes.cause: An unguarded re-run: `world_state.py:14172-14175` calls `open_evacuation_corridor(France, X)` after EVERY ratified treaty (`final_state not in ("WAR",)`, verified); the nearby gate at `:14194` does check `current_state in (WAR, ARMISTICE)`. That producer's stranded set is nation-wide, not pair-scoped (`withdrawal.py:547-568`): Davout, Murat and Ney were stranded on Swabia by Austria's truce (S14G-7), so the vassalage (Bavaria) and the non-aggression pact (Prussia) each logged an `evacuation_granted` beat; `treaty_word` returns "peace" for any non-ARMISTICE state (`withdrawal.py:94-104`); `_war_end_opening` (`dispatch.py:1749-1758`) turns that into "the war with … is over" and `_one_peace_one_line` (`:1562-1602`) merges the two; the candidate gate checks only that France is in the pair (`dispatch.py:3033`). The player (turn 6): after vassalising Bavaria and signing a non-aggression pact with Prussia the dispatch read "Sire — the war with Bavaria and Prussia is over. Davout, Murat and Ney hold under your own orders and were not moved — the treaty offers a road, it does not overrule the Emperor. Their passage lapses with the corridor."
causes.fix: Gate the `world_state.py:14172` call on `ctx.current_state in ("WAR", "ARMISTICE")` and have the opener return {} when the pair was never at war; split `ordered` into "on the treaty's road" (`is_road_home_order`) and "your own orders"; `treaty_word` gains a third word for a pair never at war (`campaign_log.py:2524-2529` defaults to "peace" the same way, and `withdrawal.py:776`).

causes.title: Talleyrand's truce reading says "−57, short of the line; the war resumes" beside a −60 rule — the bond forces the exit and the counsel rebuilt its own wording
causes.prior: sibling of PC-X61 (`70d0b475`, the bond arm), PC-F44 "the ONE wording" (`aa7eeba4`) and DDB-26 (two screens disagree on one truce) — all present; the counsel's copy of the three exits dates from PC-R2, before the bond arm existed, and no test pins the counsel line under a bond
causes.cause: The sentence is `backend/game_logic/counsel.py:822-824` (the "war" arm of the `heading` dict, built in `_truce_reading` `:808-827`): it prints "short of the line; the war resumes" for any `exit == "war"`. The −57 also omits the player's own +8-a-turn mission: `armistice_projected_relation` (`:5206-5209`) is relation + 3 × turns only (−66 → −57 over three turns) while the actual rise was +11 (−77 → −66); `war_status.py:892` and `cure_line` (`:5544-5569`, which prices "N turns of Improve Relations" with one already running) share it.

causes.title: A blocking ENEMY PHASE box says "Britain, Russia, Austria and 6 other courts stirred, but their formations remain beyond our sight" every turn at peace
causes.prior: NEW; sibling of LV-13 / PT-E4 / CA9-F7 (they collapsed the text to one sentence; the modal that carries it was never made conditional); the sentence is pinned at `tests/test_ep_f1_the_first_ten_minutes.py:492`
causes.cause: `turn_manager.py:1315` loops every non-player court (`world.enemy_nations`, `world_state.py:1913`, at war or not) and `:1406` counts every AI action (recruit, build, wait); `enemy_phase_fog.py:58-231` hides all of it that is not FULL-visible or involving France; `_build_visible_enemy_phase` (`backend/main.py:2109-2130`) then emits the single line "Britain, Russia, Austria and 6 other courts stirred, but their formations remain beyond our sight" (the visible-actions case, `:2099-2107`, appends the same sentence as `fog_hidden_nations`). `main.gd:4505-4522`: `if response.has("enemy_phase")` → `set_input_enabled(false)` and the modal (`enemy_phase_dialog.gd:104-108`). The backend returns None (no modal) only when `raw_total == 0` (`:2138`), which essentially never happens (`SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md` §40.2 records "12 of 40 turns have no visible action"). The dead branch "No enemy actions this turn" is `enemy_phase_dialog.gd:109`. The player ended turns 7 to 20 with no enemy at war with France and clicked Continue through the same sentence each time.
causes.fix: A phase with nothing visible and no `enemy_victory` returns a `fog_only` payload; `main.gd` prints one terminal line instead of raising the modal when no court shown is at war with France or in a truce; restrict the named courts to those at war with, or adjacent to, France.

causes.title: "Reassure Ally" is shut while Talleyrand courts another court; the busy sentence names the remedy but not the trade, and the alliance slid from 40 to 23
causes.prior: RETURN (partial) of S14E-11 — the fix is present (`19319041`: `slide_lever`, `mission_gate`, `_slide_counsel`) and fired; it names the lever and the remedy, it does not weigh the recall; the same root as S14G-25 (one diplomat slot)
causes.cause: `slide_lever` (`diplomacy.py:14650-14708`) reads `mission_gate` (`:14626-14647`: `mission_is_live` → "Mission already active"); `_slide_counsel` (`:14783-14786`) prints "Reassure Ally is shut while Talleyrand is at Austria's court — recall Talleyrand from Austria first (the Cabinet's Recall is free)." — S14E-11 working as built. The one-mission rule is ruled design (`DIPLOMACY_SPEC.md:369`, "Talleyrand's attention is finite"). The slide itself is universal peacetime drift, −1 a turn above +10 (`diplomacy.py:14027-14028`): 40 → 36 at turn 5 → 23 at turn 18; a 1805 alliance is born on its 40 line and frays from turn 2. The player is partly wrong ("never got a turn"): the Recall is free and one click, and they began the Austria mission three actions before opening Spain and viewed Spain once; the page never priced the trade and gives no deadline for the lapse (NOT FOUND: a France–Spain "may collapse" warning in 299 states).
causes.fix: The "busy" sentence adds each side's cost: "recalling forfeits Austria's remaining courtship (+8 a turn, N turns); Spain, at 36, drops under the 40 line in about K turns"; warn on the Improve Relations confirm when it would shut Reassure Ally for a sliding ally. The design half (S14G-D5): one slot or two.
causes.dr: Talleyrand courts one court at a time (`DIPLOMACY_SPEC.md:369`). Should "Reassure Ally" be able to run beside a courting mission, so that keeping an alliance warm and winning a new court are not the same scarce slot?

causes.title: The Admiralty's "march to the yard" link — and every Admiralty chip — names no action price: the standing march spent 2 of 4
causes.prior: sibling of S14E-26 (quote-first on priced chips — its sweep listed only the gold-priced diplomatic chips), S14E-13 (`camp_leave_line`) and DDB-61 (the blockade chip's note states its price) — all present; `naval.py` never reads `order_quotes`
causes.cause: `naval.py:4035-4042` `expedition_road_chips` builds the chip — label "Dumonceau, march to Normandy", note "6,500 men, N provinces to the yard — he embarks there" — with no price and no clock; `strategic_ledger.gd:1124-1143` `_chip_row` renders only label and note and the "do:" press sends the typed command, which becomes a standing MOVE_TO at `Marshal.strategic_order_ap()` = 2 (`marshal.py:1018-1051`; Dumonceau is cautious, not literal). No quote or ask follows (the S14E-22 detour ask fires only when the lawful road is at least twice the direct road). The tree states AP elsewhere: `region_panel.gd:1003-1005` ("Hold (2 AP)"), `:1122-1144` ("Soult · 2 AP · 3 turns" from `order_quotes.march_quote`, `order_quotes.py:342`), `strategic_executor.py:186` and the audience arm "[2 AP]". Every Admiralty chip omits AP: `naval.py:4340` (Recall), `:4390` (Blockade, 1 AP), `:4441` (Diversion, 1 AP), `:4009` (Land chips, 2 AP per `meta_executor.py:1212-1238`), `:4065` (Commission); `:4453` (Lay down ships) is gold only; the road chip also omits the camp-leave line. The player (turn 2) pressed the link (6,500 men, 4 provinces to the yard), it executed at once and spent 2 of the 4 actions — learned from the 2/4 counter.
causes.fix: Build the chip from `order_quotes.march_quote(world, marshal, yard)` — "Dumonceau · 2 AP · 4 turns" with its `camp` and `pay` lines — and add an "(N AP)" cost note to every Admiralty chip from the verb's real price. A march is cheap and cancellable, so no ask is warranted; the price at the point of choice is.

causes.title: The dispatch advises two turns of drill for a broken corps; the executor refuses drill during retreat recovery
causes.prior: sibling of FA-D9 (introduced the line, present) and CN-4 / CRT-7 (the chips and the counsel already read `drill_refusal` — `counsel.py:369`, `state_probe.py:198`, `world_state.py:211`); the dispatch prose is the one drill advice left off the predicate; same class as conquest #11 / S14G-18 and diplomacy #9 / S14G-24 (advice built without the verb's refusal predicate)
causes.cause: `dispatch.py:4503-4522` `_derive_danger`, branch 2 (verified): any corps below `MORALE_FAILING_BELOW` (40) gets "Two turns of drill would steady them (+10 morale; +15 with a training ground)", built from the drill constants alone — it never asks whether drill is open. Massena (morale 0, broken at Milan) is in retreat recovery: the refusal comes from `executor.py:2459-2491` ("recovering from retreat and cannot drill. Recovery: 2 turns remaining") and the pure predicate `tactical_executor.py:46-106` `drill_refusal` (the retreating arm `:79-81`; the adjacent-enemy arm `:96-105` also fits, Charles being one frontier away). The retreat sentence exists at `dispatch.py:4524-4526` but is branch 3, shadowed by branch 2. Siblings: `economy_executor.py:1903-1909` ("consider drilling before battle"), Teulie's identical line in the same dispatch, the Generals card's morale prose (not verified). The player's `--n` was off by one: the drill is action 60 (`frames/0060.jpg`), action 59 is Bernadotte's retreat.
causes.fix: In `_derive_danger` call `drill_refusal(world, marshal)`; when refused the tail becomes the reason and when it opens ("recovering from the rout, 2 turns — drill once he has reformed") and branch 3's retreat sentence merges into the morale line.

causes.title: The expedition's confirm card prices the throw and the failure, never the prize
causes.prior: RETURN (partial) of S14E-15 — `road_notes` is present (`19319041`) and covers a road already BEGUN; a first landing has no pointer. `NAVAL_SPEC.md` §5.2 says the Formables page lists Ireland "from day one", but no landing surface points to it
causes.cause: The confirm card (`naval_executor.py:669-697`; action 108, action 109 the same screen) lists the odds, the coverer, the failure losses, the intercept fleet action, the odds levers and the pay. The success branch (`:713-826`) is not previewed: undefended soil goes through the capture pipeline (plunder/secure), a garrison or marshal means a fight or "beachhead is contested", and a corps under 5,000 holds no homeland (`movement_executor.py:125-151`). The Ireland pointer is built by `formations.road_notes`, which skips a road with nothing held (`formations.py:1748` `if not held: continue  # not begun`); that feeds the Ulster panel line (`region_panel.gd:260-265`), the Admiralty's `expedition_notes` (`naval.py:4321-4325`) and the post-landing reply (`naval_executor.py:817-821`), so a first landing gets none. "Stripped? unknown — scout it" is the doctrine supply mark (`doctrines.py:351`), unrelated to the prize. The player (turn 6): read the "Dumonceau asks" quote before sailing for Ulster (72 in 100; the failure costs 30% lost and a decisive defeat halving every pooled fleet) and found nothing on what winning gets him; the second landing (Dumonceau under 5,000) could not hold the province, which the player learned only afterwards.
causes.fix: `road_notes` also emits a "prospect" for an unbegun carvable road, and the confirm card and the chip note gain one success clause: "Ulster is half of the Ireland carve (with Munster) — hold both while the war with Britain runs and Britain can be made to erect it at a table; what waits ashore is unscouted; under 5,000 men holds no ground." Siblings: the Munster landing, the `Land X` chips (`naval.py:3999-4008`, `region_panel.gd:695-707`), the Grand Diversion card.

causes.title: Moving the camp's main body out of the camp brings the blockade back a turn later, and neither the order nor the notice names the cause
causes.prior: RETURN (partial) of S14E-13 — `camp_leave_line` (`19319041`) is present and fired on the reply ("Orleanais lies outside the camp — this takes 30,000 men out of it; the 5-turn count resets at the turn's end."); it says the count resets, not what the staged camp was holding off; the same class as conquest #7 / #8 / #10 (an order's reply silent about the consequence it later triggers)
causes.cause: The player's action number is wrong (the order is action 134, turn 8, not 140) and its description incomplete: the reply DID carry the camp-leave line (`frames/0134.jpg`; `naval.py:2716-2719` `camp_leave_line`, stamped at `strategic_executor.py:2282-2284`). What it never says is the price. A staged camp makes `derive_ai_postures` set Britain to "guard" (`naval.py:3079`); break it and she returns to "blockade". Posture is derived at `naval.py:3613` before `_camp_tick` (`:3622`), so the return lands one turn late: turn 9's income has no Blockade line, turn 10's (action 144) shows "Blockade: −320g". The rail line then reads "Britain closes France's ports … 62%" with no cause. The lift names its cause (`_lift_cause`, `naval.py:382-393`); the return does not (`:3725-3731`). The Admiralty's staged line (`:2620-2622`) says only "resets the count"; the quote carries the same clause (`order_quotes.py:319`, `:336`). The player (turn 8) sent Soult (30,000, the main body of the Flanders camp) to "pursue Paget" two turns after the Admiralty said the camp had lifted Britain's blockade; "Soult pursues Paget. Moves to Orleanais." and, two turns on, "Blockade: −320g" again.
causes.fix: When `camp_staged` and a hostile island fleet sits in "guard", extend `camp_leave_line`: "— Britain's squadrons, held home by the camp, go back to the blockade (trade −62%, crews rot, about −320g a turn)"; name the broken camp in the `blockade_begins` notice; say the one-turn lag; the Admiralty's staged line and the quote carry the same clause.

causes.title: "March to Paris" from Flanders takes Westphalia (Prussian soil, three turns) on a tie; the road and its turns show only after the order is paid
causes.verdict: defect (the tie-break)+design+legibility (no free quote for a typed march)
causes.prior: sibling of S14E-22 (the typed march's detour ask — present, `4ac79a0f`, fires only when the direct road is closed) and conquest #10 / S14G-11 (the same "road shown after payment" class); NEW as a cause (the tie-break)
causes.cause: The frames are action 291 (Napoleon) and 290 (Soult). Flanders is not adjacent to Artois; three roads tie at three plains hops: Picardy–Artois–Paris and Picardy–Champagne–Paris (own soil) and Westphalia–Artois–Paris (Prussian soil). `find_weighted_path` (`world_state.py:6599-6665`) weighs only the destination's terrain; every tie goes to push order (the counter, `:6633`, `:6665`, verified), which is the registry adjacency order — Flanders lists Westphalia before Picardy, so Westphalia wins, onto foreign soil that feeds 15,000 for 37,692 men ("~1,231 a turn lost"). `plot_route` (`strategic.py:690-734`) prefers lawful roads, not own soil. The costs print only after the first step is taken (`strategic_executor.py:2279-2309`: supply DDB-44, campaign pay S14E-2, the camp-leave line); S14E-22's free ask does not fire because `march_detour_reading` returns None when the road equals the direct road (`strategic.py:1131-1136`); the reply gives no turn count (the player's "3 turns" is `march_turns(3, 1)`). The turn-1 road (Lorraine → Orleanais → Flanders) is a plain two-hop own-soil road, not this fault; Davout's four turns is the true distance. Siblings: `weighted_paths_from` (`world_state.py:6669`, which feeds the map's ETA tint and must keep the same tie rule — pinned by `test_cc3_select_click_enter`) and `find_path` (BFS, `:6545-6597`, PURSUE / SUPPORT).
causes.fix: A small epsilon edge cost for soil the mover neither holds nor is allied on, in `find_weighted_path` and `weighted_paths_from` together, so ties go to own soil; print "N turns" in the typed MOVE_TO reply as the PURSUE reply does.
